# Dot plots {#sec-dot-plots} :::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false} ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #02577A;"} **Requirements:** ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"} **✅ a numeric (continuous) variable** :::
::: {.cell layout-align="right"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](dot_plots_files/figure-html/full_code_display-1.png){fig-align='right' width=60% height=60%} ::: ::: :::: ## Description A dot plot displays each data point as a dot on a single axis, making it useful for identifying patterns, gaps, and outliers in small to moderate datasets. Each dot represents an observation in the data, stacked over categories or spread along a number line. In `ggplot2`, we can build dot plots with [`geom_dotplot()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/geom_dotplot.html) ## Set up ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **PACKAGES:** ::: Install packages. ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} install.packages("palmerpenguins") library(palmerpenguins) library(ggplot2) library(dplyr) # for data manipulation ``` ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **DATA:** ::: ::: {.column-margin} ![Artwork by Allison Horst](www/lter_penguins.png){fig-align="right" width="100%" height="100%"} ::: The `penguins` data ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} penguins <- palmerpenguins::penguins glimpse(penguins) #> Rows: 344 #> Columns: 8 #> $ species Adelie, Adelie, Adelie… #> $ island Torgersen, Torgersen, … #> $ bill_length_mm 39.1, 39.5, 40.3, NA, … #> $ bill_depth_mm 18.7, 17.4, 18.0, NA, … #> $ flipper_length_mm 181, 186, 195, NA, 193… #> $ body_mass_g 3750, 3800, 3250, NA, … #> $ sex male, female, female, … #> $ year 2007, 2007, 2007, 2007… ``` ::: ::: ## Grammar ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **CODE:** ::: 1. Create labels with `labs()` 2. Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data` 3. Map `flipper_length_mm` to the `x` axis 4. Add the `geom_dotplot()` layer 5. Adjust the `dotsize` ::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-fold="show"} labs_dotplot <- labs( title = "Adult foraging penguins", subtitle = "Distribution of flipper length", x = "Flipper length (millimeters)") ggp2_dotplot <- ggplot(data = penguins, aes(x = flipper_length_mm)) + geom_dotplot(dotsize = 0.5) ggp2_dotplot + labs_dotplot ``` ::: ::: ::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"} **GRAPH:** ::: ::: {.cell .column-page-inset-right layout-nrow="1"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](dot_plots_files/figure-html/create_graph_dotplot-1.png){width=576} ::: ::: A downside of using dot plots is the lack of interpretability of the `y` axis.[^dot-y-axis] [^dot-y-axis]: Read more in the [function reference.](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/geom_dotplot.html#details)
